영화관.x: I saw a movie at the theater on the weekend.
영화관.t: 극장 is also very common for 'movie theater'.

봉투.x: The convenience store clerk asked if I needed a bag.
봉투.t: Cashiers often ask "봉투 필요하세요?" ("Do you need a bag?"); in Korea bags usually cost extra.

경찰관.x: I got lost, so I asked a police officer for directions.
경찰관.t: In everyday speech people usually just say 경찰 or, politely, 경찰관님.

행사.ex: 이번 주말에 학교에서 큰 행사가 있어요.
행사.x: There's a big event at school this weekend.
행사.t: Stores also use 행사 for a sale or promotion: 할인 행사 'discount event'.

어지럽다.x: I stood up suddenly, and now I feel dizzy.
어지럽다.e: Also means 'messy, cluttered': 방이 어지러워요, 'the room is a mess.'

동시에.x: The two people raised their hands at the same time.

충분히.forms: 충분히 + verb: 충분히 쉬세요; 충분히 -(으)ㄹ 수 있다
충분히.ex: 감기에 걸리면 물을 충분히 마셔야 해요.
충분히.x: When you have a cold, you need to drink enough water.
충분히.t: 충분히 -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요 means 'you can definitely do it': 충분히 할 수 있어요!

경고.ex: 빨간 불에 길을 건너서 경찰에게 경고를 받았어요.
경고.x: I crossed on a red light and got a warning from the police.

당일.m: that day, the same day, the day itself
당일.ex: 표는 공연 당일에도 살 수 있어요.
당일.x: You can also buy tickets on the day of the show.
당일.t: 당일치기 여행 means a same-day round trip — a very common phrase.

업로드.ex: 어제 찍은 여행 사진을 블로그에 업로드했어요.
업로드.x: I uploaded the travel photos I took yesterday to my blog.
업로드.t: In casual speech, 올리다 is more common: 사진을 올렸어요.

시큰둥하다.x: I gave my younger brother a present, but his reaction was lukewarm.
시큰둥하다.t: Often describes a reaction or attitude: 반응이 시큰둥하다 'the response is lukewarm'.

청산.m: liquidation; settling (accounts or debts); clearing away (the past)
청산.ex: 그 회사는 결국 파산해서 청산 절차를 밟았어요.
청산.x: The company eventually went bankrupt and went through liquidation.
청산.e: Literally 'clear calculation' — settling everything up completely.
청산.t: Also used figuratively: 과거를 청산하다 means to break with or settle the past.

과소평가하다.ex: 상대 팀을 과소평가하면 질 수도 있어요.
과소평가하다.x: If you underestimate the other team, you might lose.

인간성.m: humanity, human nature; one's character as a person
인간성.ex: 능력도 중요하지만 인간성이 더 중요하다고 생각해요.
인간성.x: Ability matters, but I think character matters more.
인간성.t: Pronounced [인간썽]; 인간성이 좋다 'to be a decent person' is a common phrase.

객관.ex: 역사를 공부할 때는 객관과 주관을 구별해야 해요.
객관.x: When studying history, you need to distinguish the objective from the subjective.
객관.e: Literally 'a guest's view' — seeing things from outside yourself.
객관.t: Usually heard as 객관적 'objective' or 객관성 'objectivity' rather than alone.

심미적.x: This building has high aesthetic value.
심미적.t: Use 심미적 right before a noun; elsewhere use 심미적인 or 심미적으로.

지속 가능성.ex: 요즘은 기업들도 지속 가능성을 중요하게 생각해요.
지속 가능성.x: These days, companies also consider sustainability important.
지속 가능성.e: Literally 'the ability to keep going.' -성 = '-ness/-ity': 가능성, 안전성.
지속 가능성.t: 가능성 is pronounced [가능썽] — the 성 is tensed.

장담하다.m: to guarantee, to assure, to bet (that)
장담하다.ex: 이번 경기는 우리 팀이 이길 거라고 장담해요.
장담하다.x: I guarantee our team will win this game.
장담하다.t: A very common pattern is 장담할 수 없다, 'I can't guarantee it.'

청구하다.m: to claim, to bill, to demand (payment)
청구하다.x: I filed a claim with the insurance company for my hospital bills.

합헌.ex: 헌법재판소는 그 조항에 대해 합헌 결정을 내렸습니다.
합헌.x: The Constitutional Court ruled that the provision is constitutional.
합헌.e: Literally 'agreeing with the constitution'; the opposite is 위헌.
합헌.t: Pronounced [하펀] — ㅂ plus ㅎ becomes an aspirated ㅍ.

핵분열.x: Nuclear power plants generate electricity through nuclear fission.
핵분열.t: Pronounced [핵뿌녈]; 분열 alone also means a split in a group, like a political party.

지긋하다.m: advanced in years, mature; patient, steady
지긋하다.x: An elderly gentleman asked me for directions.
지긋하다.e: Mainly in 나이가 지긋하다 'of mature age'; the adverb 지긋이 means 'patiently'.
지긋하다.t: A respectful way to say 'old': 연세가 지긋하신 분 'an elderly person'.

휑하다.x: With all our stuff moved out, the house feels empty.

현모양처.m: a wise mother and good wife (traditional ideal)
현모양처.x: In the past, being a wise mother and good wife was considered the ideal for women.
현모양처.e: Literally 'wise mother, good wife' — a traditional ideal now often criticized.
현모양처.t: Today it can sound old-fashioned or sexist, so use it carefully.
